headline: Kings secure long-awaited first win, lose Quinton Byfield to upper-body injury
take:
ESPN reports the Kings broke through for their first win, a 5-2 victory over the Capitals, but lost center Quinton Byfield to an upper-body injury in the first period. Daily Faceoff reports Washington goalie Logan Thompson is day-to-day with a lower-body injury after appearing to be shaken up in the same game.

Byfield's absence would sting more than his two points in seven games so far this season suggest. LAK controlled 64% of the 5-on-5 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) while he was on the ice, and the team's share of chances rises by about 20 percentage points with him in the lineup. His own expected goals total is 1.87 against one actual goal, so a scoring bounce looked likely. Thompson's value is just as clear. He has saved 4.51 goals more than an average goalie would have against the same shots so far this season, after 28.16 over 58 games last year. WSH has otherwise been middling at 51% of 5-on-5 expected goals.

If Byfield misses time, going by how the coach has used his players, Scott Laughton (14:43 a night) is next in line for his minutes. Corey Perry, the busiest man on the second power-play unit, is the likeliest to move up to the first.
